title: Beginner
canDo: Understand and use familiar everyday expressions and very basic phrases.

units.title: Greetings & Introductions
units.description: Meet people and introduce yourself.

lessons.title: Basic Greetings
lessons.description: Common ways to greet people.
grammar: Good morning!

lessons.title: Introduce Yourself
lessons.description: Tell someone your name and ask theirs.
grammar: My name is {name}.
What is your name?
Nice to meet you.

activities.goal: Greet the person, introduce yourself and ask their name.

lessons.title: How Are You?
lessons.description: Ask and answer how someone is.
grammar: How are you?
I'm fine, thank you.

lessons.title: Please & Thank You
lessons.description: Be polite in everyday situations.

units.title: Numbers & Colors
units.description: Count, say your age and name colors.

lessons.title: How Old Are You?
grammar: I am {number} years old.
How old are you?

units.title: Family & People
units.description: Talk about your family and describe people.

lessons.title: My, Your, His, Her
grammar: This is my brother.
Her name is {name}.

lessons.title: Describing People
grammar: She is tall.
He has brown eyes.

lessons.title: Pets & Animals
grammar: I have a dog.
Do you have a pet?

units.title: Food & Drink
units.description: Order at a café and talk about what you like.

lessons.title: Drinks
grammar: A cup of tea, please.

lessons.title: I Like, I Don't Like
grammar: I like coffee.
I don't like milk.
Do you like tea?

lessons.title: At the Café
grammar: I would like a coffee.
How much is it?

activities.goal: Order a drink and a snack, then ask for the bill.

units.title: Daily Routine
units.description: Time, days and what you do every day.

lessons.title: Telling the Time
grammar: What time is it?
It's half past seven.

lessons.title: Every Day (Present Simple)
grammar: I work every day.
She works on Mondays.
He doesn't drink coffee.

units.title: At Home
units.description: Rooms, furniture and where things are.

lessons.title: There Is / There Are
grammar: There is a sofa in the living room.
There are two chairs.
Is there a garden?

lessons.title: In, On, Under
grammar: The cat is under the table.

units.title: Around Town
units.description: Places, directions, transport and shopping.

lessons.title: Asking for Directions
grammar: Where is the station?
Turn left at the corner.

activities.goal: Ask a local how to get to the museum.

lessons.title: Getting Around
grammar: I go to work by bus.

lessons.title: Shopping
grammar: Can I pay by card?
This is too expensive.

activities.goal: Ask for a different size and pay.

units.title: Free Time
units.description: Hobbies, sports and what you can do.

lessons.title: Sports
grammar: I play football on Saturdays.

lessons.title: I Can, I Can't
grammar: I can swim.
She can't drive.
Can you cook?

lessons.title: Weekend Plans
grammar: Let's go to the cinema.
Are you free on Sunday?

activities.goal: Invite a friend to do something on the weekend and agree on a time.

units.title: Weather & Clothes
units.description: Seasons, the weather and what people are wearing.

lessons.title: The Weather
grammar: It's sunny today.

lessons.title: Right Now (Present Continuous)
grammar: I am wearing a jacket.
It is raining.
What are you doing?

units.title: Yesterday
units.description: Talk about the past.

lessons.title: Was & Were
grammar: I was at home yesterday.
Were you tired?

lessons.title: Past Simple (Regular)
grammar: I watched a film last night.
She didn't work on Friday.

lessons.title: Past Simple (Irregular)
grammar: We went to the park.
Did you see the game?

activities.goal: Tell a colleague what you did last weekend and ask about theirs.

title: Elementary
canDo: Communicate in simple, routine tasks and describe your background, immediate needs and everyday plans.

units.title: Jobs & Work
units.description: Talk about jobs, workplaces and how often you do things.

lessons.title: Jobs
lessons.description: Names of common jobs.

lessons.title: What Do You Do?
lessons.description: Ask and talk about someone's job.
grammar: What do you do?
I work as a teacher.
I work for a bank.

activities.goal: Ask a new coworker about their job and describe your own.

lessons.title: Always, Often, Never
lessons.description: Say how often you do something.
grammar: I always start work at nine.
She never works on weekends.

lessons.title: At the Office
lessons.description: Everyday office vocabulary.

lessons.title: A Job Interview
lessons.description: Talk about your skills and experience.
grammar: I have three years of experience.
Why do you want this job?

activities.goal: Answer basic interview questions about your job and experience.

units.title: Comparisons
units.description: Compare people, things and places.

lessons.title: Bigger, Better, Faster
lessons.description: Compare two things.
grammar: This car is faster than that one.
My house is bigger than yours.

lessons.title: The Best & The Worst
lessons.description: Compare more than two things.
grammar: This is the best restaurant in town.
He is the tallest in the class.

lessons.title: Comparing Cities
lessons.description: Describe and compare places you know.
grammar: London is more crowded than my town.

lessons.title: As...As
lessons.description: Say two things are equal or not.
grammar: She is as tall as her brother.
This isn't as expensive as that one.

units.title: At the Shops
units.description: Quantities, supermarkets and returning items.

lessons.title: Countable & Uncountable
lessons.description: Talk about things you can and can't count.
grammar: There is some rice.
There are three apples.

lessons.title: Some & Any
lessons.description: Use some and any correctly.
grammar: Is there any milk?
There isn't any sugar.
There are some eggs.

lessons.title: Much & Many
lessons.description: Ask about quantities.
grammar: How much water do you want?
How many people are coming?

lessons.title: At the Supermarket
lessons.description: Shop for groceries.

lessons.title: Returning an Item
lessons.description: Return or exchange something you bought.
grammar: I'd like to return this.
Can I get a refund?

activities.goal: Return a broken item to the shop and ask for a refund.

units.title: Health & the Body
units.description: Body parts, symptoms and visiting the doctor.

lessons.title: How Do You Feel?
lessons.description: Describe how you feel and what hurts.
grammar: I have a headache.
My back hurts.

lessons.title: At the Doctor's
lessons.description: Explain symptoms and understand advice.
grammar: You should see a doctor.
Take this medicine twice a day.

activities.goal: Describe your symptoms to the doctor and get advice.

lessons.title: Should & Shouldn't
lessons.description: Give simple health advice.
grammar: You should drink more water.
You shouldn't work so much.

units.title: Travel Plans
units.description: Get ready for a trip and find your way around.

lessons.title: Going To
lessons.description: Talk about plans and intentions.
grammar: I'm going to visit Rome.
We're going to stay for a week.
Are you going to travel by plane?

lessons.title: At the Airport
grammar: Where is gate 12?

activities.goal: Check in for your flight and ask about your gate.

lessons.title: Finding Your Way
lessons.description: Ask for and understand directions in a new city.
grammar: Excuse me, how do I get to the hotel?
Go straight and turn right.

lessons.title: Booking a Hotel
grammar: I'd like to book a room for two nights.

units.title: The Future
units.description: Talk about the future, predictions and plans.

lessons.title: Will
lessons.description: Talk about the future with will.
grammar: I will call you tomorrow.
It will rain later.
She won't be late.

lessons.title: Making Predictions
grammar: I think it will be sunny.
People will probably travel to space.

lessons.title: Plans & Arrangements
lessons.description: Talk about things already arranged.
grammar: What are you doing this weekend?
I'm meeting my friend on Friday.

activities.goal: Talk on the phone about your plans for next week.

units.title: What Were You Doing?
units.description: Talk about actions in progress in the past.

lessons.title: Was/Were + -ing
grammar: I was cooking dinner.
They were watching TV.

lessons.title: What Were You Doing?
grammar: What were you doing at 8pm?
Were you sleeping?

lessons.title: While I Was...
lessons.description: Combine past continuous and past simple.
grammar: While I was cooking, the phone rang.
I was walking when it started to rain.

activities.goal: Tell a friend about something unusual that happened to you yesterday.

units.title: Life Experiences
units.description: Talk about things you have and haven't done.

lessons.title: Have You Ever...?
grammar: Have you ever been to Japan?
I have never tried sushi.

lessons.title: Already & Yet
grammar: I have already finished.
I haven't seen it yet.

activities.goal: Ask a friend about interesting things they have done and share your own.

units.title: Phone Calls & Emails
units.description: Communicate by phone and by email.

lessons.title: On the Phone
grammar: Can I speak to Anna, please?
Can you hold on?

lessons.title: Leaving a Message
grammar: Can I take a message?
She'll call you back later.

activities.goal: Leave a message for someone who is not available.

lessons.title: Writing an Email
grammar: Dear Mr Smith,
I am writing to ask about...

lessons.title: Invitations
grammar: Would you like to come to my party?
I'd love to, thanks!

units.title: Rules & Obligations
units.description: Talk about rules, obligations and permission.

lessons.title: Must & Mustn't
grammar: You must wear a seatbelt.
You mustn't smoke here.

lessons.title: Have To
grammar: I have to work on Saturday.
Do you have to wear a uniform?

lessons.title: Could
lessons.description: Make suggestions with could.
grammar: You could try the new restaurant.
We could go by train instead.

lessons.title: Asking Permission
grammar: Can I open the window?
Could I leave early today?

activities.goal: Ask your manager for permission to leave work early and explain why.

title: Intermediate
canDo: Deal with most situations while travelling, describe experiences and events, and give reasons and explanations for opinions and plans.

units.title: Life Experiences
units.description: Talk about experiences in more detail using present perfect and past simple together.

lessons.title: Present Perfect vs Past Simple
lessons.description: Choose between finished time and unspecified time.
grammar: I have visited Paris three times.
I visited Paris in 2019.
She has lived here for five years.

lessons.title: Since & For
lessons.description: Talk about how long something has continued.
grammar: I have worked here since 2018.
I have worked here for six years.

lessons.title: Life Achievements
lessons.description: Talk about important things you have achieved.
grammar: I have achieved a lot this year.
What is your biggest achievement?

lessons.title: Sharing Life Stories
lessons.description: Ask and answer about experiences, mixing present perfect and past simple.

activities.goal: Catch up with an old friend about what you have both done and ask for details about specific events.

units.title: Telling Stories
units.description: Use past perfect and narrative language to tell longer stories.

lessons.title: Past Perfect
lessons.description: Talk about an earlier past action.
grammar: I had already left when she arrived.
She had never seen snow before that day.

lessons.title: Past Perfect vs Past Simple
lessons.description: Show which action happened first.
grammar: When I arrived, the film had already started.
After she had finished, she went home.

lessons.title: Linking a Story
lessons.description: Connect events in a story clearly.

lessons.title: Describing a Past Experience
lessons.description: Tell a longer story about something that happened to you.
grammar: It was raining when the accident happened.

lessons.title: Telling an Anecdote
lessons.description: Share a short personal story with a partner.

activities.goal: Tell a colleague a short, surprising story about something that happened to you and react to theirs.

units.title: Opinions
units.description: Give opinions, agree, disagree and give reasons.

lessons.title: Giving Your Opinion
grammar: In my opinion, this is the best option.
I think we should wait.

lessons.title: Agreeing & Disagreeing
grammar: I completely agree with you.
I see your point, but I disagree.

lessons.title: Giving Reasons
lessons.description: Support your opinion with a reason.

lessons.title: Discussing a Topic
lessons.description: Have a short discussion and respond to another opinion.

activities.goal: Share your opinion on an everyday topic, give a reason, and respond to someone who disagrees.

units.title: Conditionals
units.description: Talk about real, possible and imaginary situations.

lessons.title: Zero & First Conditional
grammar: If it rains, we stay home.
If I have time, I will call you.

lessons.title: Using the First Conditional
grammar: If you study hard, you will pass the exam.
Unless you hurry, you'll miss the bus.

lessons.title: Second Conditional
lessons.description: Talk about imaginary or unlikely situations.
grammar: If I won the lottery, I would travel the world.
If I were you, I would apologize.

lessons.title: Real or Imaginary?
lessons.description: Choose the right conditional for the situation.

activities.goal: Talk with a friend about what you would do if you could change your job or your city.

units.title: Passive Voice
units.description: Use the passive voice in everyday situations.

lessons.title: Passive Voice (Present)
grammar: The office is cleaned every morning.
English is spoken here.

lessons.title: Passive Voice (Past)
grammar: The email was sent yesterday.
The window was broken last night.

lessons.title: Active vs Passive
lessons.description: Choose the natural form for everyday situations.

lessons.title: Passive in Everyday Life
lessons.description: Recognise the passive voice in notices, news and instructions.

units.title: Reported Speech
units.description: Report what other people said.

lessons.title: Reported Statements
grammar: She said that she was tired.
He told me he would call later.

lessons.title: Reported Questions
grammar: She asked me where I lived.
He asked if I was coming.

lessons.title: Reporting a Conversation
lessons.description: Report what someone said to you earlier.

activities.goal: Tell a friend what your manager said in a meeting you both missed.

units.title: Relative Clauses
units.description: Describe people and things with relative clauses.

lessons.title: Who, Which, That
grammar: The woman who called is my manager.
This is the book that I told you about.

lessons.title: Where & Whose
grammar: That's the café where we met.
He's the man whose car was stolen.

lessons.title: Defining People & Things
lessons.description: Give extra information about people, places and objects.

lessons.title: Describing Someone You Know
lessons.description: Describe a person you know using relative clauses.

units.title: Work & Careers
units.description: Apply for jobs, join meetings and talk about your career.

lessons.title: Applying for a Job
grammar: I'm applying for the position of manager.
I meet all the requirements.

lessons.title: Interview Skills
lessons.description: Talk in more detail about your strengths and experience.
grammar: My main strength is problem-solving.
I was responsible for the whole team.

lessons.title: At a Meeting
grammar: Let's move on to the next point on the agenda.
I'd like to add something.

lessons.title: Career Changes
grammar: I've decided to change careers.
She got promoted last month.

lessons.title: Talking About Your Career
lessons.description: Discuss your career goals and a recent challenge with a colleague.

activities.goal: Discuss your career goals and a recent challenge at work with a colleague.

units.title: Health & Lifestyle
units.description: Give advice and talk about habits, past and present.

lessons.title: Should & Ought To
grammar: You should eat more vegetables.
You ought to see a doctor.

lessons.title: Used To
lessons.description: Talk about past habits that have changed.
grammar: I used to smoke, but I quit.
She didn't use to exercise.

lessons.title: Giving Lifestyle Advice
lessons.description: Give someone advice about changing their lifestyle.

activities.goal: Give a friend advice about improving their sleep and diet, using should, ought to and used to.

units.title: Media & Technology
units.description: Talk about news, social media and modern technology.

lessons.title: Social Media Habits
grammar: I spend too much time scrolling through my phone.

lessons.title: Talking About Technology
grammar: We rely on technology more than ever.
I need to upgrade my phone.

lessons.title: Pros & Cons of Technology
lessons.description: Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of modern technology.

activities.goal: Discuss the pros and cons of social media with a friend and share your own opinion.

title: Upper Intermediate
canDo: Understand complex texts, interact with fluency and spontaneity, and produce clear, detailed text on a wide range of subjects, explaining a viewpoint on a topical issue.

units.title: Regrets & Hypotheticals
units.description: Talk about the past you can't change and imagine how things could have been different.

lessons.title: Third Conditional
lessons.description: Talk about imaginary past situations and their imaginary results.
grammar: If I had studied harder, I would have passed the exam.
If she hadn't left early, she wouldn't have missed the train.

lessons.title: Mixed Conditionals
lessons.description: Combine past causes with present results and present causes with past results.
grammar: If I hadn't taken that job, I wouldn't be living here now.
If she were more organized, she would have finished on time.

lessons.title: Wish & If Only
lessons.description: Express regrets and wishes about the past and present.
grammar: I wish I had studied medicine.
If only I had more free time.
I wish I could speak French.

lessons.title: Expressing Regret
lessons.description: Talk naturally about things you regret and could have done differently.
grammar: I should have listened to my parents.
I shouldn't have quit my job so soon.

lessons.title: Talking About Regrets
lessons.description: Share a personal regret and discuss what you would do differently.

activities.goal: Tell a friend about something you regret and what you wish you had done differently.

units.title: Deduction & Speculation
units.description: Guess what happened or what is true using modal verbs of deduction.

lessons.title: Must, Might, Can't
lessons.description: Make guesses about the present using modal verbs.
grammar: He must be tired after that flight.
She can't be at home, the lights are off.

lessons.title: Must Have, Might Have, Can't Have
lessons.description: Make guesses about the past.
grammar: They must have left already.
She can't have forgotten the meeting.
He might have missed the bus.

lessons.title: Speculating About Situations
lessons.description: Speculate about unclear or surprising situations.
grammar: I bet she forgot about the appointment.
Presumably, the flight was delayed.

lessons.title: Discussing a Mystery
lessons.description: Use deduction to work out what happened in a mysterious situation.

activities.goal: Discuss with a friend what you think happened to a missing neighbour, using modals of deduction.

units.title: Passive & Causative
units.description: Use advanced passive structures and talk about services done for you.

lessons.title: Passive With Modals
lessons.description: Use the passive voice with modal verbs.
grammar: The contract must be signed by Friday.
This problem should be solved quickly.

lessons.title: It Is Said That...
lessons.description: Report general beliefs and facts impersonally.
grammar: It is said that the company is losing money.
The bridge is believed to be over 200 years old.

lessons.title: Have/Get Something Done
lessons.description: Talk about services someone else does for you.
grammar: I'm having my car repaired tomorrow.
We got the kitchen redecorated last month.

lessons.title: Arranging a Service
lessons.description: Ask someone to arrange a service for you.

activities.goal: Call a company to arrange for something in your home to be repaired and agree on a time.

units.title: Talking About the Future
units.description: Predict, plan and imagine what will be happening or finished by a certain time.

lessons.title: Future Continuous
lessons.description: Talk about actions in progress at a point in the future.
grammar: This time next week, I will be lying on a beach.
Don't call at 9, I'll be sleeping.

lessons.title: Future Perfect
lessons.description: Talk about actions that will be finished before a future point.
grammar: By next year, I will have finished my degree.
She will have left before we arrive.

lessons.title: Future Forms Review
lessons.description: Choose the right future form for the situation.

lessons.title: Predicting Long-Term Changes
lessons.description: Make predictions about long-term trends and changes.
grammar: In ten years, most cars will have become electric.

lessons.title: Talking About Your Future
lessons.description: Discuss your own long-term plans and predictions with a partner.

activities.goal: Discuss with a friend what you think your life will be like in ten years.

units.title: Linking Ideas
units.description: Connect ideas clearly when writing or arguing a point.

lessons.title: However, Whereas, Although
lessons.description: Use linking words to show contrast.
grammar: The hotel was expensive; however, the service was excellent.
Whereas he prefers the city, she prefers the countryside.

lessons.title: Despite & In Spite Of
lessons.description: Contrast ideas using a noun or -ing form.
grammar: Despite the rain, we went for a walk.
In spite of his age, he still runs every day.

lessons.title: Cause & Result
lessons.description: Link causes and results in writing.
grammar: Due to the strike, all flights were cancelled.
Prices rose; as a result, sales fell.

lessons.title: Structuring an Argument
lessons.description: Organise ideas clearly in a short piece of writing or a spoken argument.

units.title: Advanced Reported Speech
units.description: Report what people said using a wider range of reporting verbs.

lessons.title: Suggesting, Advising, Warning
lessons.description: Report suggestions, advice and warnings.
grammar: She suggested going to the cinema.
He warned me not to be late.

lessons.title: Promising, Refusing, Admitting
lessons.description: Report promises, refusals and admissions.
grammar: He promised to call me back.
She admitted making a mistake.

lessons.title: Reporting With Modals
lessons.description: Report sentences containing modal verbs.
grammar: He said he could help later.
She said she might be late.

lessons.title: Retelling a Conversation
lessons.description: Retell a longer conversation using a variety of reporting verbs.

activities.goal: Tell a friend about an argument you overheard, reporting what each person said.

units.title: Phrasal Verbs at Work
units.description: Use common phrasal verbs and collocations in a professional setting.

lessons.title: Phrasal Verbs for Meetings
lessons.description: Common phrasal verbs used in meetings and projects.
grammar: Let's bring up that issue at the next meeting.
We need to follow up with the client.

lessons.title: Dealing With Workload
lessons.description: Talk about managing tasks and deadlines.
grammar: I've fallen behind on my emails.
Stop putting off that report.

lessons.title: Business Collocations
lessons.description: Common word partnerships used at work.
grammar: We finally reached an agreement with the supplier.

lessons.title: Discussing a Project
lessons.description: Discuss the progress of a work project using phrasal verbs and collocations.

activities.goal: Update a colleague on a project's progress, using phrasal verbs and business collocations.

units.title: Debate & Persuasion
units.description: Hedge, concede points and build a persuasive argument.

lessons.title: Hedging Your Opinion
lessons.description: Soften opinions so they sound less direct.
grammar: It could be argued that remote work reduces productivity.
To some extent, I agree with you.

lessons.title: Conceding a Point
lessons.description: Accept part of the other side's argument before disagreeing.
grammar: Admittedly, the plan has some risks, but it's worth trying.
Having said that, we still need more evidence.

lessons.title: Persuasive Language
lessons.description: Use language that persuades and convinces.
grammar: Surely you can see the benefits of this plan.
There's no doubt that we need to act now.

lessons.title: Having a Debate
lessons.description: Take part in a structured debate on an everyday issue.

activities.goal: Debate an everyday issue with a friend, hedging your opinion and conceding at least one point.

units.title: Society & the Environment
units.description: Discuss social issues and environmental challenges.

lessons.title: Environmental Issues
lessons.description: Talk about problems facing the environment.
grammar: We need to reduce carbon emissions.
More cities are investing in renewable energy.

lessons.title: Social Issues
lessons.description: Discuss issues affecting society.
grammar: The government is trying to raise awareness of homelessness.

lessons.title: Possible Solutions
lessons.description: Suggest solutions to social and environmental problems.
grammar: The city plans to tackle traffic congestion by building more bike lanes.

lessons.title: Discussing a Global Issue
lessons.description: Share your views on an environmental or social issue with someone else.

activities.goal: Discuss a current environmental issue with a friend and suggest possible solutions.

units.title: Science, Culture & the Arts
units.description: Describe trends, explain causes and effects, and talk about art, culture and discoveries.

lessons.title: Describing Trends
lessons.description: Describe rises, falls and trends using appropriate vocabulary.
grammar: Sales rose sharply after the new product launched.
The number of users has remained stable this year.

lessons.title: Cause & Effect
lessons.description: Explain how one event leads to another.
grammar: Overfishing has led to a sharp decline in fish populations.
The new policy resulted in lower unemployment.

lessons.title: Scientific Discoveries
lessons.description: Talk about scientific breakthroughs and discoveries.
grammar: Scientists have discovered a new way to store energy.

lessons.title: Art & Culture
lessons.description: Describe works of art, films and cultural events.
grammar: The exhibition features some thought-provoking contemporary art.

lessons.title: Discussing a Cultural Event
lessons.description: Talk about a film, exhibition or performance you have seen.

activities.goal: Tell a friend about a film or exhibition you saw recently and give your opinion of it.

title: Advanced
canDo: Understand a wide range of demanding, longer texts and recognise implicit meaning. Express ideas fluently and spontaneously, and use language flexibly for social, academic and professional purposes.

units.title: Inversion & Emphasis
units.description: Put weight on what matters with inverted word order and cleft sentences.

lessons.title: Negative Adverbials
lessons.description: Invert subject and auxiliary after negative and restrictive adverbials.
grammar: Never have I seen such a beautiful sunset.
Rarely does the board reject a proposal outright.

lessons.title: Only, No Sooner, Not Until
lessons.description: Use inversion after "only", "no sooner", "hardly" and "not until".
grammar: No sooner had we sat down than the power went out.
Only after the results came in did we realise the scale of the problem.
Not until she left did I understand how much she had done.

lessons.title: Inverted Conditionals
lessons.description: Drop "if" and invert in formal conditional sentences.
grammar: Had I known about the delay, I would have rebooked the flight.
Should you require further assistance, please contact us.
Were it not for your support, the project would have collapsed.

lessons.title: Cleft Sentences
lessons.description: Focus attention with it-clefts and wh-clefts.
grammar: It was the lack of funding that ended the project.
What I find most striking is the speed of the change.
All he did was complain.

lessons.title: Emphasising a Point
lessons.description: Stress a view with fronting and emphatic structures in a lively conversation.

activities.goal: Tell a friend about a surprising event, using inversion and cleft sentences for emphasis.

units.title: Hypotheticals & the Subjunctive
units.description: Handle complex conditions, wishes and formal suggestions with precision.

lessons.title: Complex Conditionals
lessons.description: Combine conditions across time and use "but for" and "otherwise".
grammar: But for her advice, I would still be working in a job I hated.
If he hadn't been so stubborn, we would be partners by now.

lessons.title: Were To, Happen To, Should
lessons.description: Talk about remote or tentative possibilities.
grammar: If the company were to relocate, would you go with it?
If you happen to see Mark, could you pass on the message?

lessons.title: The Subjunctive
lessons.description: Use the present subjunctive after verbs and adjectives of demand and importance.
grammar: The committee recommended that he be given a second chance.
It is essential that every employee complete the training.

lessons.title: Wishes & Preferences
lessons.description: Express regret, irritation and preference with "wish", "would rather" and "it's time".
grammar: It's high time we changed the way we work.
I'd rather you didn't mention it to anyone.
He talks as though he owned the place.

units.title: Advanced Grammar Structures
units.description: Command the passives, participle clauses and noun phrases of formal English.

lessons.title: Complex Passives
lessons.description: Use passive infinitives, perfect passives and get-passives.
grammar: The painting is thought to have been stolen in the 1970s.
He objected to being treated like a child.

lessons.title: Participle Clauses
lessons.description: Condense information with -ing, -ed and perfect participle clauses.
grammar: Having reviewed the data, the team changed its approach.
Built in 1890, the station is now a museum.
Judging by the reviews, the film is well worth seeing.

lessons.title: Nominalisation
lessons.description: Turn verbs and adjectives into nouns for a formal, compact style.
grammar: The rapid decline of local newspapers has changed how people follow politics.
Their reliance on a single supplier proved costly.

lessons.title: Ellipsis & Substitution
lessons.description: Avoid repetition with "do so", "the former", "the latter" and reduced clauses.
grammar: Employees may leave early, but few choose to do so.
Both plans are risky; the former is cheaper, the latter faster.

units.title: Hedging & Discourse
units.description: Sound careful, tactful and well organised when you speak and write.

lessons.title: Hedging Language
lessons.description: Soften claims with hedges, so you sound cautious rather than blunt.
grammar: The findings would seem to suggest that the effect is relatively small.
It could be argued that the policy has largely failed.

lessons.title: Discourse Markers
lessons.description: Signal contrast, addition, concession and consequence in extended talk.
grammar: The results were promising; that said, the sample was small.
Be that as it may, we still need to cut costs.

lessons.title: Concession
lessons.description: Grant a point while keeping your own, with "however", "much as" and "albeit".
grammar: Much as I admire her, I can't support the proposal.
It was a useful, albeit expensive, solution.

lessons.title: Disagreeing Tactfully
lessons.description: Disagree, correct and criticise without causing offence.

lessons.title: Steering a Discussion
lessons.description: Take the floor, redirect a conversation and summarise the main points.

activities.goal: Chair a short discussion, disagree tactfully with a colleague and steer the group back to the agenda.

units.title: Professional Life
units.description: Communicate with authority in meetings, negotiations and reports.

lessons.title: Negotiating Terms
lessons.description: Make offers, set conditions and reach compromise.
grammar: We'd be prepared to lower the price, provided you commit to a longer contract.
Were you to increase the order, we could offer a discount.

lessons.title: Managing & Leading
lessons.description: Delegate, motivate and give constructive feedback.
grammar: I'd suggest you take ownership of the client relationship going forward.

lessons.title: Reports & Proposals
lessons.description: Describe trends, recommend action and write in a professional register.
grammar: Sales plummeted in the third quarter before levelling off.
In light of these findings, it is recommended that the scheme be extended.

lessons.title: Change & Conflict at Work
lessons.description: Talk through restructuring, disagreements and resolving tension.

lessons.title: The Senior Interview
lessons.description: Present your experience with confidence in an interview for a senior role.

activities.goal: Answer an interviewer's questions about your track record, your leadership style and a difficult decision you made.

units.title: Media & Information
units.description: Analyse how news is made and how messages persuade.

lessons.title: News & Headlines
lessons.description: Read between the lines of headlines and reports.
grammar: The minister is reported to have resigned.

lessons.title: Bias & Spin
lessons.description: Talk about how language shapes opinion.
grammar: The story was framed in such a way as to blame the council.

lessons.title: Social Media & Privacy
lessons.description: Discuss online behaviour, data and digital footprints.
grammar: Were platforms held liable, they might moderate content more carefully.

lessons.title: Assessing Sources
lessons.description: Weigh up the reliability of claims, statistics and sources.
vocabulary: take with a pinch of salt

activities.goal: Challenge a friend's claim about an online story, questioning the source and the statistics.

units.title: Science, Technology & Ethics
units.description: Explain innovation and debate where it should stop.

lessons.title: Research & Methods
lessons.description: Describe how studies are designed and what findings show.
grammar: The study found no evidence that the two variables were causally linked.

lessons.title: AI & Automation
lessons.description: Discuss what intelligent machines mean for work and society.
grammar: Were more tasks to be automated, entire professions might disappear.

lessons.title: Ethical Dilemmas
lessons.description: Argue about right and wrong in medicine, technology and business.
grammar: Scientists ought not to be allowed to act without independent scrutiny.

lessons.title: Debating Innovation
lessons.description: Weigh the benefits and risks of a new technology in a debate.

activities.goal: Argue for or against a controversial new technology, respond to objections and propose safeguards.

units.title: Society & Environment
units.description: Talk about inequality, policy and the planet in depth.

lessons.title: Social Inequality
lessons.description: Discuss wealth, opportunity and social mobility.
grammar: Not only has inequality widened, but it has also become more entrenched.

lessons.title: Climate & Sustainability
lessons.description: Talk about climate policy, carbon and the transition to renewable energy.
grammar: Had governments acted earlier, the worst effects might have been avoided.

lessons.title: Politics & Governance
lessons.description: Discuss how societies are governed and how policy is made.
grammar: It is the electorate who ultimately decide, not the pundits.

lessons.title: Community Action
lessons.description: Persuade others to take part in a local or global cause.

activities.goal: Persuade a neighbour to join a local campaign, explaining the problem, the plan and why their help matters.

units.title: Idioms & Collocations
units.description: Sound natural with fixed phrases and word partnerships.

lessons.title: Strong Collocations
lessons.description: Pair verbs, nouns and adjectives the way native speakers do.
grammar: The report raises serious concerns about safety standards.

lessons.title: Idioms of Work & Money
lessons.description: Use idioms about effort, risk, cost and success.

lessons.title: Idioms of People & Feelings
lessons.description: Describe character, mood and relationships with idioms.
vocabulary: at the end of my tether
wear your heart on your sleeve

lessons.title: Advanced Phrasal Verbs
lessons.description: Master less common, sometimes idiomatic phrasal verbs.
grammar: Let's iron out the remaining details before the launch.

lessons.title: A Story With Idioms
lessons.description: Tell an anecdote and colour it with idioms and collocations.
vocabulary: by the skin of my teeth

activities.goal: Tell a friend about a day when everything went wrong, using at least four idioms naturally.

units.title: Argument & Academic Writing
units.description: Build a case in formal writing and speech.

lessons.title: Structuring an Essay
lessons.description: Write introductions, thesis statements and topic sentences.
grammar: This essay will argue that public transport deserves greater investment.

lessons.title: Evidence & Citation
lessons.description: Refer to sources and data accurately and fairly.
grammar: These findings corroborate earlier research by Chen (2019).

lessons.title: Counterarguments
lessons.description: Acknowledge opposing views and rebut them.
grammar: Critics contend that the tax is unfair; however, this overlooks its long-term benefits.

lessons.title: Presenting a Case
lessons.description: Deliver a structured, persuasive mini-presentation and answer questions.

activities.goal: Present an argument on a topic of your choice and respond to a sceptical question from the audience.

title: Proficiency
canDo: Understand virtually everything heard or read, summarise information from different sources and express yourself spontaneously, very fluently and precisely, differentiating finer shades of meaning even in the most complex situations.

units.title: Register & Nuance
units.description: Choose exactly the right word and tone for every audience.

lessons.title: Formal & Informal Registers
lessons.description: Shift between casual, neutral and highly formal English without a slip.
grammar: I would be grateful if you could confirm receipt of this letter.
Let me know if you can make it.

lessons.title: Connotation & Shades of Meaning
lessons.description: Tell apart near-synonyms that carry different attitudes.
grammar: She's not stubborn, she's resolute; there's a difference.

lessons.title: Euphemism & Understatement
lessons.description: Say difficult things gently, or say less than you mean.
grammar: The results were not entirely what we had hoped for.
He's a touch over-enthusiastic, shall we say.

lessons.title: Regional & Social Varieties
lessons.description: Recognise British, American and other varieties, slang and dialect.

lessons.title: Adjusting Your Tone
lessons.description: Rephrase a message for a boss, a friend and a stranger.

activities.goal: Deliver the same awkward news first to a close friend and then to a senior client, adjusting register and tact.

units.title: Modality & Stance
units.description: Convey certainty, doubt, attitude and obligation with fine control.

lessons.title: Modal Nuances
lessons.description: Use "may well", "might as well", "needn't have" and "was to have" with precision.
grammar: You may well be right, but I'd like to check first.
We needn't have hurried; the train was late.
The talks were to have ended on Friday, but they dragged on.

lessons.title: Stance Adverbials
lessons.description: Signal your attitude to what you say with sentence adverbs.
grammar: Ostensibly a charity, the organisation was in fact a lobbying group.
Understandably, the staff were reluctant to speak.

lessons.title: Certainty & Doubt
lessons.description: Grade your confidence from near-certain to sceptical.
grammar: In all likelihood, the vote will be postponed.
It stands to reason that prices will rise if supply falls.

lessons.title: Attitude in Conversation
lessons.description: Express reservations, reluctant agreement and gentle scepticism in a live exchange.
vocabulary: I wouldn't go so far as to say

activities.goal: Respond to a friend's ambitious plan with measured doubt, partial agreement and constructive advice.

units.title: Idiom & Figurative Language
units.description: Understand and use metaphor, idiom and proverb the way native speakers do.

lessons.title: Metaphor & Simile
lessons.description: Read and craft vivid comparisons.
grammar: Her argument was a house of cards, ready to collapse at the first challenge.

lessons.title: Opaque Idioms
lessons.description: Decode idioms whose meaning cannot be guessed from the words.
vocabulary: let the cat out of the bag

lessons.title: Proverbs & Sayings
lessons.description: Recognise proverbs and adapt them to the situation.
vocabulary: every cloud has a silver lining

lessons.title: Idioms in Context
lessons.description: Judge when an idiom enriches your speech and when it grates.

lessons.title: Figurative Storytelling
lessons.description: Tell a story rich in imagery and idiom.

activities.goal: Tell a friend about a turning point in your life, using vivid imagery and idiom without overdoing it.

units.title: Rhetoric & Persuasion
units.description: Move an audience with the devices of great speakers.

lessons.title: Rhetorical Devices
lessons.description: Recognise and use triads, parallelism, antithesis and rhetorical questions.
grammar: We came, we saw, we conquered.
Ask not what your country can do for you; ask what you can do for your country.

lessons.title: Persuasive Structures
lessons.description: Build appeals using emphasis, contrast and repetition.
grammar: The question is not whether we can afford to act, but whether we can afford not to.
vocabulary: the question is not whether but

lessons.title: Emotive Language
lessons.description: Spot how word choice manipulates feeling and how to use it responsibly.

lessons.title: Writing a Speech
lessons.description: Open strongly, build to a climax and close memorably.

lessons.title: Delivering a Speech
lessons.description: Deliver a short persuasive speech and respond to an interruption.

activities.goal: Deliver a short speech using at least three rhetorical devices, then deal with a hostile interruption gracefully.

units.title: Humour, Irony & Wordplay
units.description: Get the joke and make your own.

lessons.title: Irony & Sarcasm
lessons.description: Tell verbal irony, sarcasm and dry understatement from sincerity.
grammar: Oh, brilliant. Another meeting that could have been an email.

lessons.title: Puns & Wordplay
lessons.description: Understand double meanings, puns and playful language.

lessons.title: British Humour
lessons.description: Grasp self-deprecation, banter and understatement in British comedy.
grammar: That's a bit rich coming from someone who's never been on time.

lessons.title: Telling a Funny Story
lessons.description: Time a punchline, build comic tension and land the joke.

activities.goal: Tell a friend a funny, slightly embarrassing story with good timing, then respond to their teasing in kind.

units.title: Academic & Formal Writing
units.description: Write with the precision, distance and structure of scholarly prose.

lessons.title: Academic Register
lessons.description: Use impersonal constructions, precise verbs and careful qualification.
grammar: It can be inferred from the data that consumer confidence remained fragile.
The outcome is contingent on a number of interrelated factors.

lessons.title: Cohesion in Long Texts
lessons.description: Link paragraphs with reference, lexical chains and signposting.
grammar: The policy reduced costs, thereby freeing resources for research.

lessons.title: Summarising & Paraphrasing
lessons.description: Condense long arguments and restate ideas in your own words.

lessons.title: Critical Evaluation
lessons.description: Judge the strength of an argument and its methodology.
grammar: While the conclusions are compelling, the methodology is not beyond criticism.

lessons.title: Formal Correspondence
lessons.description: Write and respond to formal letters, complaints and proposals with authority.
vocabulary: I am writing with regard to

activities.goal: Present a formal complaint to a company's representative, cite the facts and negotiate a satisfactory resolution.

units.title: Literature & Style
units.description: Read literary English closely and write with style.

lessons.title: Literary Vocabulary
lessons.description: Understand words used in fiction, poetry and essays.

lessons.title: Narrative Voice & Tone
lessons.description: Distinguish narrator, viewpoint and tone in a text.
grammar: He paused. Surely she must have known? The whole town certainly did.

lessons.title: Stylistic Variation
lessons.description: Vary sentence length, syntax and rhythm for effect.
grammar: Silence. Then, slowly, without a word, the door began to open.

lessons.title: Discussing a Book
lessons.description: Analyse themes, characters and style in a work of literature.

activities.goal: Discuss a novel you know with a fellow reader, analysing its themes and style and defending your interpretation.

units.title: Ideas & Philosophy
units.description: Discuss abstract concepts and reason about them with clarity.

lessons.title: Abstract Concepts
lessons.description: Talk about freedom, justice, identity and meaning.
grammar: What we call freedom is, to a large extent, a matter of perspective.

lessons.title: Logic & Fallacies
lessons.description: Name flawed reasoning and reason soundly.
grammar: That doesn't follow; it's a classic non sequitur.

lessons.title: Thought Experiments
lessons.description: Pose and follow hypothetical scenarios.
grammar: Were we to accept that premise, it would follow that no one is responsible.

lessons.title: A Philosophical Discussion
lessons.description: Explore a big question and test each other's reasoning.
vocabulary: it depends on what you mean by

activities.goal: Explore an abstract question with a friend, define your terms, challenge each other's assumptions and reach a considered view.

units.title: Culture, Language & Identity
units.description: Reflect on how language, tradition and belonging shape who we are.

lessons.title: Language Change
lessons.description: Discuss how English evolves, spreads and borrows.
grammar: Rather than corrupting a language, borrowing has always been how it grows.

lessons.title: Identity & Belonging
lessons.description: Talk about heritage, migration and cultural identity with sensitivity.
grammar: For many, identity is less a fixed fact than an ongoing negotiation.

lessons.title: Cross-Cultural Communication
lessons.description: Navigate differences in politeness, directness and etiquette.

lessons.title: Traditions & Modernity
lessons.description: Discuss what to preserve and what to change.

activities.goal: Discuss with a friend from another culture which traditions are worth preserving, and how customs differ between your countries.

units.title: Mastery & Mediation
units.description: Use English as a fluent, flexible professional and mediator.

lessons.title: Interpreting & Reformulating
lessons.description: Relay complex ideas clearly for people who need a simpler or different version.
grammar: What the report is really saying is that the plan is unworkable.

lessons.title: Difficult Conversations
lessons.description: Deliver bad news, defuse conflict and rebuild trust.

lessons.title: Thinking on Your Feet
lessons.description: Answer unexpected questions, buy time and recover from a slip.
vocabulary: off the top of my head

lessons.title: Chairing & Moderating
lessons.description: Lead a panel, manage speakers and sum up a complex debate.

activities.goal: Moderate a panel discussion, draw out quiet speakers, manage a heated exchange and summarise the key positions.
